title: A triple protostar system formed via fragmentation of a gravitationally unstable disk
question: Does the disk around the triple protostar system L1448 IRS3B show evidence of gravitational instability and fragmentation forming the tertiary companion?

data.sensitivity: 0.14 mJy/beam continuum; 15 mJy/beam per 0.25 km/s channel

evidence.quote: $D$ = 230 pc(cite: hirota2011) is the distance to the Perseus molecular cloud

recipe.method: CASA clean after manual calibration and self-calibration; continuum Briggs robust 0.5, lines natural with 500 klambda taper; uv>50 klambda

recipe.goal: Subtract tertiary IRS3B-c in uv plane
recipe.method: Fit point source plus extended Gaussian with constant offset in 0.7x0.6 arcsec ellipse using imfit; model Fourier transformed with setjy and subtracted with uvsub

recipe.goal: Derive disk inclination and position angle
recipe.method: Single Gaussian fit to image tapered to 0.43x0.36 arcsec with center fixed on IRS3B-a; inclination = arccos(minor/major)

recipe.goal: Estimate disk and IRS3B-c masses from dust
recipe.method: Optically thin isothermal dust mass equation, M=D^2 F/(kappa B(T))
key_parameters: T_dust = 30 K disk, 40 K for IRS3B-c; kappa 0.899 or 2.3 cm2/g

recipe.method: Deproject visibilities, image, measure flux in annuli of half-beam width centered on IRS3B-a, convert to surface density
assumptions: Radial temperature profile from Section 6 model

recipe.method: Draw Keplerian curve on C18O PV diagram along major axis at 45.4 deg inclination; compare with thin-disk model

recipe.goal: Toomre Q and cooling time analysis
recipe.method: 1D analytic disk models: Q, t_cool, radiative-equilibrium temperature with irradiation and accretion heating, for a range of accretion rates
key_parameters: Each protostar 0.5 Msun; f≈0.1; opacity 0.24 cm2/g or ~T^2; 1 Myr Baraffe radii
assumptions: Accretion rate benchmark 1e-7 Msun/yr from L=3.2 Lsun

evidence.quote: the position angle is 29.5$^\circ$ east of north
we find $M_{\rm disk}=0.30~M_{\odot}$ using the integrated 1.3 mm flux density of 0.52 $\pm$ 0.002 Jy
the mass of IRS3B-c in the outer disk is estimated to be 0.085 $M_{\odot}$ from the 1.3 mm flux density of 0.19 $\pm$ 0.003 Jy
We find that the combined mass for both IRS3B-a and IRS3B-b is likely $\sim$1.0 M$_{\odot}$.

answer_key.quantity: Deprojected separations of b and c from a

evidence.quote: The deprojected separations of IRS3B-b and IRS3B-c from IRS3B-a are 78 AU and 254 AU, respectively.
the disk around IRS3B is marginally unstable ($Q\approx1$) at radii between 150 AU and 320 AU
the fragment mass ranges from $0.005-0.015\mbox{M$_{\odot}$}$ between $150-320$ AU

score_reason: Public single-EB data and clear mass recipe, but clean/selfcal and Keplerian-mass details missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public data, numeric results (inclination, masses, flux densities) reproducible with described steps.
